name: Separate MCP protocol and execution errors
summary: Preserve the distinction between malformed protocol requests and recoverable tool failures.
when_to_use: An MCP adapter hides failures or retries every failure identically.
prerequisites: A declared MCP protocol revision and captured example responses.
instructions: Classify unknown tools and malformed requests as protocol failures.
Return tool execution failures with isError=true and concise corrective context.
Keep error classification visible through adapters; redact credentials.
Choose retry behavior from the failure cause, not from HTTP success alone.
verification: A missing tool produces a protocol error; an invalid business value produces an execution error.
Neither fixture is recorded as a successful task result.
limitations: The channel distinction is specified; adapter design and retry policy are synthesis. No implementation was exercised.
host_scope: MCP implementations using the named protocol revision.

name: Choose tool eligibility per workflow stage
summary: Make tool selection explicit without confusing selection controls with authorization.
when_to_use: A workflow selects irrelevant tools or omits a prerequisite lookup.
prerequisites: A tool inventory, stage-specific permitted operations, and an executor that can enforce authorization.
instructions: For each stage, declare whether no tool is valid, which lookup is required, and which operations are eligible.
Map those requirements to documented selection controls when available; otherwise expose only eligible tools through a gateway.
Enforce execution authorization independently of model selection.
If a required lookup did not succeed, stop dependent actions and report the unmet prerequisite.
Evaluate ambiguous requests, no-tool requests, and disallowed operations before rollout.
applicable_standards: Application tool-selection policy and executor authorization contract.
verification: A no-tool fixture completes without an unnecessary call.
A required-lookup fixture cannot reach the dependent action without its evidence.
A disallowed operation remains denied even if the model requests it.
limitations: Selection controls and request fields vary by API. The neutral stage policy is synthesis from the cited provider example; no adapter was run.
host_scope: Agent workflows with a tool executor and stage-specific capability routing.

name: Verify MCP HTTP authorization boundaries
summary: Check discovery, audience binding, and scope failures before integrating a protected MCP server.
when_to_use: An HTTP MCP connection needs OAuth or repeatedly fails authorization.
prerequisites: An HTTP MCP endpoint and its selected authorization implementation.
instructions: Record the protocol revision and discover protected-resource and authorization-server metadata.
Use the resource parameter and validate that received tokens target this server.
Implement PKCE and prevent token passthrough to downstream services.
Handle insufficient scope with a bounded reauthorization path; keep credentials out of logs.
applicable_standards: MCP 2025-11-25 authorization; RFC 9728 metadata; RFC 8707 resource indicators.
verification: A wrong-audience token is rejected.
A missing-scope request follows the intended challenge path.
Repeated authorization failures terminate instead of looping.
limitations: This HTTP flow does not apply to stdio credential loading. Checklist synthesis; no OAuth exchange was run.
host_scope: Protected HTTP MCP clients and servers.

name: Route file work through available built-in tools
summary: Select search, read, edit, and shell capabilities from the actual session inventory.
when_to_use: A coding agent uses broad shell commands for narrow file tasks or assumes unavailable tools.
prerequisites: The current host's tool inventory and permission rules.
instructions: Inspect the available tool inventory and permission boundaries.
Use file-name search to locate candidates and content search to locate relevant text.
Read relevant content, make a targeted edit, and inspect the resulting diff.
Use shell execution for builds, tests, and capabilities absent from dedicated tools only when shell access is permitted.
If neither a dedicated tool nor an authorized command can perform a step, report the missing capability and stop that step.
applicable_standards: Observed tool inventory, local permissions, and repository command conventions.
verification: A search fixture locates the expected file and text.
An edit fixture changes only the intended content.
The route works with the observed inventory.
limitations: Tool names and availability vary. The routing procedure is inferred from the cited tool reference; no live runner compatibility was tested.
host_scope: Coding agents with authorized file inspection and editing capabilities.

name: Verify scoped instruction loading
summary: Check that conditional rules load for matching files and stay absent elsewhere.
when_to_use: Monorepo rules leak across components or fail to activate.
prerequisites: A declared path-to-guide mapping and a runner with either conditional loading diagnostics or an explicit document router.
instructions: Define a focused guide, its path scope, and a harmless marker that can establish whether it was loaded.
With conditional loading, configure the documented path rules and record how path roots are resolved.
Open a matching file in a fresh session and inspect loader diagnostics or the supplied context for the guide.
Repeat with a nonmatching file in another fresh session and confirm that the guide is absent.
If automatic loading cannot be observed, route guides explicitly from the task brief and record which guide was read; label automatic loading unverified.
applicable_standards: Runner instruction-loading contract; explicit path-to-guide routing.
verification: Matching and nonmatching fixtures produce the intended guide selection.
The check distinguishes observed loading from an agent claim that it remembers a rule.
Unavailable automatic loading is reported rather than presented as verified.
limitations: Instruction loading is context routing, not access enforcement. The procedure is synthesized from the cited implementation; no loader was exercised.
host_scope: Runners with observable conditional instruction loading or an explicit document router.

name: Build a bounded CI review job
summary: Define an event-driven review with explicit privileges, limits, and observable results.
when_to_use: Agent review must run unattended in a repository pipeline.
prerequisites: A CI runner, a noninteractive agent entry point, scoped credentials, and an accepted review scope.
instructions: Choose an event and give the job a concrete review scope and output contract.
Set minimum job permissions and obtain credentials through the CI secret or identity mechanism.
Enforce a runtime timeout externally and any supported usage limits in the agent adapter; reject unsupported interactive requests.
Follow repository dependency-pinning policy and review executable action or runner code.
Keep required deterministic checks separate from model review and retain both outcomes.
If a noninteractive run cannot report failure or be cancelled, stop deployment of the review job.
applicable_standards: CI job permission and timeout contracts; repository dependency-pinning policy.
verification: A permitted event starts the job and an excluded event does not.
The timeout cancels excessive work and preserves a failure record.
A missing permission fails without hanging on a prompt.
Failing deterministic checks remain failing even if the model approves.
limitations: This is a synthesized workflow design, not a deployed job. Model tool eligibility is separate from job credentials and repository protections.
host_scope: CI systems with a bounded noninteractive agent runner.

name: Build a representative few-shot example set
summary: Demonstrate the intended output with examples that cover real judgments and edge cases.
when_to_use: Instructions alone produce inconsistent labels, formats, or boundary judgments.
prerequisites: An output contract and examples whose expected answers can be checked.
instructions: Select a typical case, a boundary case, and an insufficient-information case when relevant.
Pair each input with an accepted output using consistent delimiters.
Vary incidental details so the examples do not accidentally teach an irrelevant shortcut.
Keep evaluation cases outside the prompt; compare results before and after adding examples.
applicable_standards: Example-based prompting and held-out evaluation against an explicit output contract.
verification: All examples satisfy the same output contract.
Held-out cases expose whether the examples improve the intended behavior.
No evaluation item appears in the prompt.
limitations: No universal example count or guaranteed accuracy gain is claimed; held-out evaluation is synthesized guidance.
host_scope: Model prompting workflows that accept examples and can be evaluated on held-out cases.

name: Validate structured MCP tool results
summary: Declare and validate the schema of server-produced tool data.
when_to_use: Consumers parse tool prose or silently accept malformed structured results.
instructions: Declare an outputSchema when consumers rely on a stable structure.
Return conforming structuredContent.
Also provide serialized JSON in a text block for backward compatibility.
Validate results before consumers use them.
applicable_standards: MCP 2025-11-25 Tools: Structured Content and Output Schema.
verification: A malformed result fails client validation.
Structured and text representations encode the same data.
limitations: Server-produced structuredContent differs from schema-constrained model generation. No live interoperability test was performed.

name: Handle schema output, refusal, and incompletion separately
summary: Validate generated data without treating every response as a successful schema instance.
when_to_use: A structured-output consumer crashes on refusals or accepts semantically wrong data.
prerequisites: An output schema, domain constraints, and an adapter that distinguishes successful, refused, incomplete, and failed responses.
instructions: Map documented response states into explicit success, refusal, incomplete, and failure outcomes.
Parse complete successful output and validate it against the schema; use constrained generation only where supported.
Check domain constraints such as allowed identifiers and numeric bounds.
Represent incompatible input explicitly, bound repair attempts, and keep final failure visible.
If response completion cannot be established, withhold downstream actions and report an unresolved result.
applicable_standards: Application output schema and response-state adapter contract.
verification: Fixtures for success, refusal, incompletion, and a semantically invalid object reach distinct outcomes.
Invalid domain data never reaches the action executor.
limitations: Schema conformity does not establish truth. Provider response fields and schema support vary; this neutral validation policy is synthesis and was not executed.
host_scope: Model-output consumers with schema validation and explicit response-state handling.

name: Reconcile batch results by request identity
summary: Account for every asynchronous batch request without relying on output ordering.
when_to_use: Many independent model requests can complete outside an interactive turn.
prerequisites: An asynchronous execution service or worker queue and a durable manifest of unique request identifiers.
instructions: Assign a unique request identifier and retain the mapping from identifier to input.
Submit requests using the service adapter and persist batch or job identifiers.
At completion, collect successful results, errors, and unresolved requests from every documented result channel.
Join by request identity, detect missing or duplicate identifiers, and preserve successful outputs.
Retry only eligible failed or unfinished items with linked attempt records.
If the service cannot correlate results to inputs, run requests individually with recorded job identities or stop batch execution.
verification: Shuffled outputs still map to the correct inputs.
Every manifest ID is successful, failed, or explicitly unresolved.
A retry excludes completed successes.
limitations: Wire formats, result channels, limits, and expiration behavior vary by service. The neutral reconciliation policy is inferred from the cited batch example; no batch was submitted.
host_scope: Asynchronous model APIs and worker queues with durable request correlation.

name: Propagate failures through dependent tool steps
summary: Preserve a failed dependency as failure instead of converting it into empty data or success.
when_to_use: A multi-step agent continues with invented values after a lookup or tool failure.
prerequisites: A dependency map and tool-call correlation identifiers.
instructions: Preserve call identity, error category, safe diagnostics, and verified partial results.
Map each tool result to the documented adapter success or failure envelope without converting errors to successful empty values.
Mark dependent steps blocked until their required inputs are available.
Continue independent branches only when their own prerequisites hold.
Report partial completion and unresolved causes; retry within a declared budget.
If an adapter cannot expose reliable failure status, stop dependent side effects and record the result as unresolved.
applicable_standards: Tool adapter result contract and application dependency policy.
verification: A failed lookup never becomes an empty successful lookup.
A dependent mutation is not invoked after its input fails.
An independent branch may finish while the final report still exposes the failure.
limitations: Dependency blocking and retry budgets are harness design choices, not guarantees supplied by the model or API.
host_scope: Agent pipelines with correlated tool calls and explicit success or failure outcomes.

name: Route uncertain findings to evidence-based review
summary: Use missing evidence and contradictions to decide what needs human review.
when_to_use: An agent is tempted to fill evidence gaps with a confident answer.
prerequisites: An agreed evidence requirement and an identified reviewer or escalation route.
instructions: Require a supporting source for each consequential claim.
Allow an explicit insufficient-evidence outcome.
Record missing facts, contradictory sources, and the decision those gaps affect.
Resolve gaps through targeted retrieval; send unresolved decision-relevant items to the reviewer.
Present a concise evidence packet and proposed next step.
applicable_standards: Evidence sufficiency, citation verification, and explicit review routing.
verification: An unsupported claim is removed, qualified, or escalated.
The reviewer can trace each disputed claim to evidence.
A confident tone alone never satisfies the evidence requirement.
limitations: The review route is synthesized. A model's verbal confidence is not established here as a calibrated probability.

name: Track provenance through multi-source synthesis
summary: Connect claims to source versions, transformations, and responsible reviewers.
when_to_use: A synthesis combines sources whose origin, date, or interpretation may differ.
prerequisites: Accessible source documents and stable identifiers for claims and source versions.
instructions: Record each source entity with its origin, version or retrieval date, and relevant locator.
For each claim, record source references and whether the claim is stated or inferred.
Record the synthesis activity and responsible agent or reviewer.
Keep conflicting claims visible and explain the basis for any resolution.
Preserve derivation links when a summary replaces the source text.
applicable_standards: W3C PROV-DM concepts: entities, activities, agents, and derivation.
verification: A reviewer can trace each consequential claim to a specific source version.
Changing a source identifies which derived claims need review.
Unresolved conflicts remain explicit.
limitations: This lightweight ledger adopts PROV concepts; it does not claim full PROV serialization or conformance.
host_scope: Research, retrieval, and multi-agent synthesis workflows.

name: Reconcile live state when resuming a session
summary: Resume the intended conversation and verify external state before continuing its plan.
when_to_use: Work spans sessions and files, branches, or external records may have changed.
prerequisites: A recorded objective, remaining work, and either saved session access or a durable handoff.
instructions: Select the intended saved session using its documented identifier; if unavailable, start a new session from the durable handoff.
Confirm the objective, working directory, and source revision.
Read current changes and the latest relevant external state.
Compare them with the saved plan and identify completed, invalidated, or ambiguous steps.
Continue from reconciled state and record a new checkpoint; pause ambiguous external side effects for review.
applicable_standards: Session adapter contract and live-state reconciliation policy.
verification: The selected session is the intended task.
Changes made since the prior session are acknowledged.
A completed external action is not repeated solely because the saved plan was stale.
limitations: Restoring a conversation does not verify external state or undo side effects. The neutral reconciliation procedure is inferred from the cited session example; no session was resumed.
host_scope: Long-running tasks with saved sessions or durable handoff records.

name: Bound code exploration and preserve evidence
summary: Explore a concrete code question while preserving source evidence across compaction.
when_to_use: Repository exploration repeats searches or loses findings as context grows.
prerequisites: A code question, search tools, and persistent notes.
instructions: Declare the code question, relevant subsystem, exploration budget, and stopping condition.
Search names and symbols, then read relevant definitions, callers, and tests.
Record findings with source locators, revision identity, uncertainty, and unanswered questions.
At the budget boundary, summarize supported findings and the next targeted search.
Before compaction or a session handoff, preserve the evidence map; afterward, reopen critical sources and check for changes.
applicable_standards: Progressive retrieval, evidence checkpoints, and bounded repository exploration.
verification: A fresh session recovers the question, findings, source locations, and remaining gaps from the checkpoint.
Changed source content invalidates the affected finding.
Budget exhaustion produces a bounded partial result.
limitations: Budgeting and evidence-map fields are synthesized guidance. No compaction or session-restoration runtime was tested.
host_scope: Coding agents with file search and persistent notes; context compaction is optional.
